_source: ColdFusion Short, watched in the built-in browser 2026-11-18: frames at 0/0.5/1/2/3/5 s then every 5-10 s to the end, word timings from YouTube's transcript panel (about 190 words a minute). Our own descriptions. 52K views. Cut from a long video plus a reused news-reporter segment.

hook.firstFrame: black frame: white title box at the top, the product name and year in big white italic condensed type in the middle
hook.firstLine: Asks you to imagine a whole smartphone sold for a few dollars.

shots.picture: black, title box top, product name and year as a big italic label centre
the boxed phone fades up behind the label, then close footage of the box
macro footage of the white phone with a big rupee price in a circle
the phone's launch web page with the price
TV news anchor and a launch event where a man holds up the phone
city street footage, a big figure in yellow italic slides over it; a government programme page
screenshots of a government digital programme site, scrolling
a phone's opened back and parts, then launch-event footage
the phone cut out on a red geometric graphic background
a tech reporter's on-camera segment from another outlet
close footage of the phone's screen and copied app icons
news footage of the founder being questioned

lines.gist: imagine a full phone selling for the price of a snack
a startup promised it, and it became the most searched phone
pre-orders poured in, and the company wanted billions in state support
the pitch: cheap phones for a national connectivity drive
each unit lost money even after ads; the launch showed the truth
it was a rebadged import with the old brand painted over, copied icons
the deal collapsed, orders never shipped, the founder was charged

whyItWorks: The absurd price is the hook and is given at once; the mystery is how it could work.
Per-unit loss is the turn: a small, concrete number that makes the scam obvious.
The reveal is physical (paint over another brand), shown in close-up.
